scenarios.title: Clothes on Fire
scenarios.description: A candle sets your sleeve on fire. What do you do?
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! When clothes catch fire, every second counts: stop, drop, and roll.

choices.text: Run to find help
choices.feedback: Running feeds the flames with more air. Stop, drop, and roll instead.

choices.text: Stop, drop, and roll
choices.feedback: Correct. Rolling smothers the flames. Cover your face with your hands while you roll.

choices.text: Wave your arm in the air
choices.feedback: Waving fans the flames and makes the fire grow.

scenarios.title: Grease Fire
scenarios.description: The oil in your frying pan bursts into flames.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! For a grease fire, cover the pan with a lid and turn off the heat.

choices.text: Pour water on the burning pan
choices.feedback: Water makes burning grease splash and spread the fire.

choices.text: Cover with a lid, turn off heat
choices.feedback: Correct. Covering the pan cuts off the oxygen. Leave the lid on until the pan is cool.

choices.text: Carry the burning pan outside
choices.feedback: Carrying a burning pan can spill flames and burn you.

scenarios.title: Trapped by Fire
scenarios.description: Flames block the hallway outside your upstairs bedroom. You have a window.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! If you are trapped, close the door, block the gaps, call for help, and signal from the window.

choices.text: Open the door and run through flames
choices.feedback: Running through fire causes severe burns and smoke inhalation.

choices.text: Seal the door and signal at the window
choices.feedback: Correct. A closed door slows smoke and fire, and signalling helps rescuers find you.

choices.text: Hide under the bed until it passes
choices.feedback: Hiding makes you harder for rescuers to find.

scenarios.title: Trapped Car
scenarios.description: Your car is trapped in rapidly moving floodwater, and water is now rising inside it.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! If water rises inside a trapped car, get on the roof and signal for help.

choices.text: Stay in the seat and wait it out
choices.feedback: Once water is rising inside the car, staying put is no longer safe.

choices.text: Get on the roof and signal for help
choices.feedback: Correct. Stay in the car while trapped by moving water, but if water rises inside, get on the roof and signal for help.

choices.text: Open the door and swim to the bank
choices.feedback: Do not swim through floodwater. Moving water is far stronger than it looks.

scenarios.title: Flash Flood Warning at Camp
scenarios.description: You are camping near a creek and a flash flood warning arrives.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! In a flash flood warning, move to higher ground immediately. Leave your gear behind.

choices.text: Pack up the tents and gear first
choices.feedback: Flash floods rise in minutes. Gear can be replaced, you cannot.

choices.text: Move to higher ground right now
choices.feedback: Correct. Get away from the creek and uphill immediately.

choices.text: Wait to see if the creek really rises
choices.feedback: Waiting for proof can leave you with no time to escape.

scenarios.title: Crossing on Foot
scenarios.description: You must cross a street covered by fast-moving, ankle-deep water.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Do not walk through moving floodwater. Turn around and find another way.

choices.text: Cross quickly because it is shallow
choices.feedback: Even a few inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet.

choices.text: Turn around and take another route
choices.feedback: Correct. Turn Around, Don't Drown. Floodwater can also hide hazards and be contaminated.

choices.text: Hold a friend's hand and cross together
choices.feedback: Two people can still be swept away. Avoid the water.

scenarios.title: Mobile Home Warning
scenarios.description: A tornado warning is issued and you are in a mobile home.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! A mobile home is not safe in a tornado. Get to a sturdy shelter right away.

choices.text: Hide in the bathtub with a mattress
choices.feedback: Mobile homes can overturn in strong winds, even when tied down.

choices.text: Go to a sturdy building or shelter
choices.feedback: Correct. Do not stay in a mobile home. Go to a nearby sturdy building, preferably one with a basement.

choices.text: Stay by the door to watch the sky
choices.feedback: Watching wastes time and exposes you to flying debris.

scenarios.title: Warning at the Office
scenarios.description: The tornado sirens go off while you are inside a large office building.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Go to the lowest floor, to an interior room or hallway away from windows.

choices.text: Go to the lowest floor, away from windows
choices.feedback: Correct. More walls between you and the outside means more protection.

choices.text: Go to the top floor for a better view
choices.feedback: Upper floors give less protection. Shelter on the lowest floor instead.

choices.text: Gather in the big open cafeteria
choices.feedback: Avoid large open rooms such as cafeterias, gyms, and auditoriums.

scenarios.title: Thunder in the Open
scenarios.description: You hear thunder while standing in an open field. A hard-topped car is nearby.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! When thunder roars, go indoors. A hard-topped vehicle is the next best choice.

choices.text: Shelter under the tallest tree
choices.feedback: Lightning often strikes tall objects, and trees are dangerous shelter.

choices.text: Lie flat in the middle of the field
choices.feedback: Lying flat in the open does not protect you. Get to a building or hard-topped vehicle.

choices.text: Get in the car and close windows
choices.feedback: Correct. A building is best, and a hard-topped vehicle with windows up is the next best option.

scenarios.title: Shaking in Bed
scenarios.description: You wake up at night as the room begins to shake violently.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! If you are in bed, stay there and protect your head and neck with a pillow.

choices.text: Run outside through the dark house
choices.feedback: Moving during shaking risks falls and injury from broken glass and debris.

choices.text: Stay in bed and cover your head
choices.feedback: Correct. Staying put and covering your head reduces your risk of injury.

choices.text: Stand in the doorway to be safe
choices.feedback: A doorway does not protect you in modern buildings. Doors can swing and hurt you.

scenarios.title: Shaking While Driving
scenarios.description: The road starts shaking while you are driving near buildings and overpasses.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Pull over in a clear area, set the parking brake, and stay in the car.

choices.text: Speed up to get away from the shaking
choices.feedback: Driving fast on damaged roads can cause a serious crash.

choices.text: Stop beneath the nearest overpass
choices.feedback: Overpasses, bridges, and buildings can collapse or drop debris.

choices.text: Pull over in the open and stay inside
choices.feedback: Correct. Stop away from buildings, trees, overpasses, and power lines, set the parking brake, and stay in the car until the shaking stops.

scenarios.title: Caught Outside
scenarios.description: You are walking beside tall buildings when an earthquake strikes.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Move to an open area away from buildings, then get down low until the shaking stops.

choices.text: Run inside the closest building
choices.feedback: Falling glass and debris near buildings cause many injuries.

choices.text: Move away from buildings, then cover
choices.feedback: Correct. Open space away from buildings, trees, and wires is safest outdoors. Get down low until the shaking stops.

choices.text: Stand still beside the nearest wall
choices.feedback: Walls and facades can fall outward onto the street.

scenarios.title: Choking Baby
scenarios.description: A baby is choking, cannot cry, and is turning blue.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! For a choking infant, give 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts, and call for help.

choices.text: Give 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts
choices.feedback: Correct. Alternate back blows and chest thrusts until the object comes out or the baby can breathe.

choices.text: Give the baby some water to wash it down
choices.feedback: Liquid can make choking worse because the airway is blocked.

choices.text: Hold the baby upside down and shake
choices.feedback: This can injure the baby and push the object deeper.

scenarios.title: Bleeding Through the Bandage
scenarios.description: A deep cut is bleeding heavily and blood is soaking through the cloth you are pressing on it.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Keep firm pressure on the wound and add more layers. Do not remove the cloth.

choices.text: Lift the cloth to check the wound
choices.feedback: Lifting the cloth disturbs the clot and lets bleeding start again.

choices.text: Add more cloth and keep pressing
choices.feedback: Correct. Keep firm pressure, add layers if needed, and call emergency services.

choices.text: Rinse the wound and leave it open
choices.feedback: Heavy bleeding must be controlled first with direct pressure.

scenarios.title: Scalded Arm
scenarios.description: Boiling water spills onto your friend's forearm.
scenarios.timeoutFeedback: Time's up! Cool a burn right away under cool running water. Do not use ice or butter.

choices.text: Put ice directly on the burn
choices.feedback: Ice can damage the skin further. Use cool running water instead.

choices.text: Hold it under cool running water
choices.feedback: Correct. Clean, cool running water cools the burn and helps relieve pain. Seek medical help for serious burns.

choices.text: Spread butter over the burn
choices.feedback: Butter and other greasy substances can seal in the heat and make the burn worse.
